speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in the last five years, whether there are employers repatriating injured migrant workers against their will due to high healthcare costs and, if so, how many of such instances have there been; (b) how many complaints have been received in the past five years relating to the employer’s failure to furnish a letter of guarantee, thereby impeding healthcare access for migrant workers; (c) what actions have been taken against such errant employers; and (d) what steps are taken to ensure that migrant workers are educated about laws and entitlements relating to their healthcare needs and the scope of their insurance coverage in their native language.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Injured workers must be certified medically fit to fly, before being repatriated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Therefore, this prevents workers with serious injuries from being repatriated before they are treated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers are also prohibited from repatriating migrant workers whose presence in Singapore is required to process their work injury or salary claims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM holds employers liable to pay for their migrant worker’s medical expenses incurred in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers may claim the medical expenses from these insurance plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For medical emergency cases, the hospitals will proceed even without LOGs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Workers are not denied such treatment regardless of their employer’s ability to pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For non-emergency cases, hospitals may ask for LOG before treatment, to be assured that the employer knows and is able to pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For the vast majority of these cases, the employers paid up shortly after administrative actions were taken by MOM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The remaining employers who failed to pay were prosecuted under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM educates new migrant workers about their employment rights and protections under Singapore law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: And this is done via the Settling-In-Programme, or SIP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The SIP is conducted in the workers’ native languages to aid understanding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It covers workers’ entitlements to insurance coverage, healthcare access and work injury compensation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM has also produced a guide for migrant workers, in their native languages, on how to seek medical help and provided contact information of MOM and NGOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Workers may also use the 24/7 telemedicine service in the FWMOMCare mobile application to consult doctors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: At any time, workers may contact MOM about any employment issues through the reporting service on MOM website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Workers are also informed to alert Immigration and Checkpoints Authority officers at immigration checkpoints if their employer attempts to repatriate them when they have a pending work injury or salary claim.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just one supplementary question relating to the hotline.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned that MOM has a hotline, a web service that migrant workers can use to raise these kinds of complaints about healthcare or other issues, and that awareness is raised about that when they initially come into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if this hotline or complaint service is widely used and is there any level of comfort that the migrant workers are comfortable with using this hotline and this appeal service, whether it is on the web or by phone?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Because a lot will depend on the migrant workers coming forward to highlight these abuses; no one else may be aware of them at the point when these things happen.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I do not have the numbers with me so I cannot comment on what the rates are at this point.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Member can always file a Parliamentary Question (PQ).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What I can say is this, beyond the hotline, workers can always call the hotline but there is also the FWMOMCare app, in which they can do more than just report.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They can also get telemedicine consultation service from doctors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, they can walk into any hospital and make a report, or work through any of the NGOs that are available.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I know of many NGOs today who are very active on the ground.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Migrant Workers' Centre (MWC), for example, has migrant worker ambassadors too, among their peers, about 5,000 of them, who can also take feedback.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If they stay in a dormitory, they can also report to the dorm operators and we will take those on board.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, we have the Forward Assurance and Support Team or FAST teams which are very active on the on ground within the dorms; so they can report to any of our officers to inform them of some of the challenges.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there are two things: one, you can reach out but the nearest is the FWMOMCare app and through which the workers can also receive telemedicine service.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, beyond just reporting, the workers can also receive telemedicine assistance.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Both ways, to some extent, compared to a few years ago before these developments, I think today, we got a lot more coverage than before.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I mentioned, we are also reviewing the medical insurance coverage for the workers too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the problem really comes in when it is non-emergency cases, where, as the Senior Minister of State had mentioned, they need the LOG.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am just wondering whether MOM would review that requirement as well so that the migrant workers can get access to medical treatment as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, the requests come under the hospitals because they would like to be assured that the employers can pay.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, for me personally, I do not think that this is needed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, the hospitals have a very different view.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is something we will continue to work through with the hospitals, to assure them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, these are things that we have to work through because I know hospitals too are concerned.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They have to ascertain first that it is a work injury – that is one part to it.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, whether it is work injury or injury caused by something else.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And secondly, the employers should be notified as well when their worker gets injured.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But let us work through to see how we can make it more seamless for the workers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have a follow-up question in relation to what the hon Senior Minister of State stated regarding the developing of an insurance programme to deal with the 5% of employers saddled with big hospital bills, particularly unexpected large medical bills.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I note from the MOM's Addendum to the President's Address that this is a matter that is under consideration.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I filed a PQ which was up for answer on the 4 January 2021.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And the hon Minister for Manpower mentioned that she is looking into this as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My question is, when can we expect a response from MOM?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Because on the ground, this seems to be an issue, particularly given the fact that we are in the midst of a COVID-19 pandemic and there would be situations where workers would need treatment, particularly with ICU stay and all these things, it can add up to quite a bit, beyond the $15,000 threshold.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Senior Minister Zaqy Mohamad, I understand that Second Minister Dr Tan See Leng also wants to provide a clarification.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: And then, I will move on to the next question.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I do not have a deadline that I can commit at this point.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I would let Dr Tan See Leng take over for further comments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If you recall in my speech last week, when I talked about the Migrant Worker Onboarding Centre, one of the key attributes of this centre is to set up an enhanced comprehensive medical examination and screening centre.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Inherent in this enhanced medical screening and examination centre would be elements of the medical screening that would incorporate a detailed history-taking as well as examination to ascertain whether the migrant worker has any pre-existing chronic conditions or pre-existing medical conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is envisaged that with that, as part of an overall comprehensive review, we will then be able to also price in the risks more accurately and more precisely with the underwriting by the different insurance companies that we have been working with.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have already engaged quite a number of insurance companies locally to help us come up with the underwriting of these premiums.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To the additional point about the number of individuals that needed hospitalisation beyond a certain level – I think the number was $15,000 – Members of Parliament would be happy to note that so far, we have been able to keep the population relatively well managed for large hospital bills, the large majority, that means 95% of them do not exceed this amount.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I hope that addresses the concerns that our colleagues have.
